findings.claim: moduleOrder places jdbc-data-access (F23 rows) before reporting-indexes-and-review, whose first four topics are F22 SQL (subqueries/CTEs, window functions, indexes, EXPLAIN). Relative to the F23 project and F24 review the order is sound (the bridge precedes jdbc-data-access-project and jdbc-review and depends only on F19-F20 SQL and the Java course), but it breaks the intake rule that modules follow calendar day order: course navigation runs SQL -> Java (F23 bridge) -> SQL (F22) -> Java (F23 project), separating the bridge's final 'Next: the F23 JDBC data access project' from the project brief by four F22 pages. The reporting module.json note that the project brief teaches JDBC concepts 'no earlier page covers' is now stale.
findings.recommendation: Keep the F23 bridge adjacent to the project brief: in a follow-up course/module change split reporting-indexes-and-review so F22 topics precede jdbc-data-access and the project brief and F24 review follow it (or move the F22 topics into an earlier module); until then, record the accepted calendar inversion in the intake and update the stale reporting module.json note in its module branch.
